details: For every finite binary class, the minimum degree of its 1-inclusion graph is at most its effective range.
proof: Every vertex of the 1-inclusion graph has at most one neighbor per effective coordinate. In particular its minimum degree is at most \mathrm E(\mathcal H).
name: Effective Range / Minimum Degree
witness_verification: For #classes/halfintervals with n>=4, the established endpoint values or bounds, in parameter order, are $n-1$ and $1$. The first parameter divided by one plus the second tends to infinity. Thus no reverse affine-linear bound holds. See the database-owned endpoint value proofs.
